name: Flesh for Lulu
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Flesh for Lulu came out of Brixton squats in eyeliner and a Stonesy swagger, got a song into a John Hughes movie and limousines on Paramount's tab, then came apart in a Sydney studio just as American college radio caught up.

hero.by: Nick Marsh and Kevin Mills in San Francisco, February 1987. Photo: Andwhatsnext, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Squats, a junkie guitarist and a pop deal
eras.text: Nick Marsh had the voice, a Fender Jazzmaster and no interest in paying rent. Polydor signed him and James Mitchell as a white-boys-do-disco act; then a strung-out Wasted Youth guitarist and a Specimen bassist from the Batcave turned it into a rock'n'roll band.

years.h: James Mitchell brings a guitar to Brixton and leaves as the drummer
years.p: Nick Marsh needs a drummer, not a guitarist. Mitchell, a drama student from Linlithgow who has never played drums, sits at a borrowed kit, and Marsh says, "OK, let's do it."
years.xp:
The name came from Lulu, Mitchell's old flatmate, standing in front of a poster for Andy Warhol's Flesh for Frankenstein. Early demos with Glen Bishop on bass were, in Louder's words, a bit Simple Minds, a bit Talking Heads.

The first gig was at Mitchell's university. Girls from the Gypsy Hill squats in Crystal Palace did the band's make-up, and it stayed in the show.

yt: Live at the Ace, Brixton, June 1983
years.h: A John Peel session lands a Polydor deal
years.p: Polydor pays for demos and signs Marsh and Mitchell, hoping for a pop duo.

years.h: Rocco Barker's dealer hands him the Melody Maker ad
years.p: The Wasted Youth guitarist owes money, so his dealer shows him a 'guitarist wanted' ad. [[Rocco Barker|6bae12ee-6fc5-402f-871a-fc34c1e1063a]] auditions on a borrowed guitar, and the others ask Marsh why he wants a junkie.
years.xp:
Marsh made getting him clean a mission. The band toured Norway because they'd heard there was no heroin there, and Barker went cold turkey in the back of the van. "I had to hold on to this shivering, gibbering wreck for a couple of weeks," Marsh told Louder's Scott Rowley.

"Within a year I was clean," Barker says. He never went back.

years.h: Roman Candle sounds nothing like what Polydor signed
years.p: Twanging guitars and chain-gang backing vocals instead of synth-pop. It reaches No. 100 in the UK and gets good reviews, which makes it hard for Polydor to drop the band.

years.h: Kevin Mills sees them at the Batcave and wants the bass job
years.p: Mills runs the Soho club night with [[Specimen|3ee1304c-1790-4b43-8e1f-4f32dbf150bd]]. He thinks the band is great apart from the bass player; Glen Bishop leaves for Under Two Flags and Mills takes over.
years.xp:
Mills soon managed and tour-managed the band too, pushing out manager Peter Webber, who later directed Girl with a Pearl Earring. All four agree the bassist-as-manager setup was a mistake. "It nearly killed me," Mills says. "I was a bit of a tyrant."

Barker had his own reason to be wary: the woman who helped him off heroin was Mills's ex.

years.h: Kevin Mills is on the cover of a debut he doesn't play on
years.p: Session man Phil Spalding finishes the bass parts. Sounds gives it four and three-quarter stars out of five; the album sells little, and Polydor drops the band.

years.cap: Flesh for Lulu on stage in Germany, 1984
years.h: Opening for the Sisters of Mercy across the UK
years.p: The support tour puts Flesh for Lulu in front of goth crowds, a label they spend years trying to shake.
years.xp:
Barker, a former junior fencing squad member, says Andrew Eldritch once challenged him to a duel at Glasgow University. Barker, with a bad ankle and a walking stick, says he won. "I fucking thrashed him."

Marsh also claimed Siouxsie Sioux copied the ripped-fishnet top he wore to the Batcave. Rowley asked Steve Severin to confirm it and got no reply.

eras.title: Nuns, Olympic Studios and the golden age
eras.text: Dropped by Polydor, the band went indie on Glasgow's Statik and made the records fans rate highest. They were warm and Stonesy where the goth pack was cold, and too country and soul for Kerrang. Beggars Banquet signed them next.

years.h: Two kissing nuns get Blue Sisters Swing banned
years.p: The cover of the five-song Hybrid EP got it banned in the US and Europe, per Wikipedia. Christian protesters turned up at American shows.
years.xp:
Barker says he found the picture in a book and Marsh hand-coloured it. Rowley traced it to Le Rêve claustral, a 1952 painting by Clovis Trouille, not the old engraving the band thought.

"We were like, 'Who are they protesting against?'" Mitchell says. "Oh, us."

years.h: Craig Leon cuts Big Fun City at Olympic Studios
years.p: Leon produced the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]]' debut and Suicide, so the band wanted him. He records the backing tracks live; Mills writes the first single, 'Baby Hurricane'.

years.cap: Flesh for Lulu in a Hybrid Records promo shot, c. 1985
years.h: A whole set of country and Cajun covers in Holland
years.p: Bus tapes from writer Kris Needs seep in, and one night the band plays Bobby Charles and Hank Williams's 'Lost Highway' instead of their own songs.

years.src: Louder · flesh4lulu.co.uk · Wikipedia: Flesh for Lulu
years.h: Beggars Banquet signs them, and Del Strangefish joins
years.p: The home of [[Bauhaus|0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201]] and [[The Cult|8846e4ff-0c19-4af2-872b-7a8dc7497f68]] puts out the Idol EP. Derek Greening of Peter and the Test Tube Babies comes in on guitar so Marsh can stop playing on stage.

eras.title: Hollywood calling
eras.text: Beggars wanted a big American-sounding record, and John Hughes wanted British alternative bands for his soundtracks. Flesh for Lulu got both: Abbey Road with Mike Hedges, a Capitol deal in the US, and a song in Some Kind of Wonderful.

years.cap: Rocco Barker and Nick Marsh at the Beacon Theatre, New York
years.h: Some Kind of Wonderful premieres, and the band plays the after-show
years.p: Mitchell writes 'I Go Crazy' on a new 4-track for the John Hughes film. After a Paramount-backed US tour with the March Violets, they play the Palace in LA on premiere night.
years.xp:
The Palace crowd, per the LA Times, included Hughes, Molly Ringwald, Andrew McCarthy, the Bangles, the Beastie Boys and Rutger Hauer. On Paramount's tab it was limousines and five-star hotels; back home in Brixton they had padlocks on their fridges, Greening says.

Producer Stephen Hague tried for a co-writing credit over one changed chord, Mitchell says; the band took it to two musicologists. Mitchell had written it darker; Marsh rewrote the lyrics for Hollywood.

q: Nick Marsh, on day one with Hedges
years.h: Mike Hedges records Long Live the New Flesh at Abbey Road
years.p: Three months in Studio 2, aimed squarely at American radio, and released by Capitol in the US. It becomes their biggest seller, and Joe Perry calls it his album of the year.
years.xp:
Mills's 'Postcards from Paradise' was later covered by Paul Westerberg, as a hidden track on Stereo (2002), and by the Goo Goo Dolls.

Marsh never warmed to the sound. An album, he told Rowley, is a bit like a tattoo: he'd been carrying it around for years.

years.cap: Marsh on stage in San Francisco, 1987
years.h: Nick Marsh puts the guitar down and becomes Nick Nasty
years.p: Marsh wants to front the band like [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]]. Tour manager Ivor Wilkins adds 'the harsh Marsh', which Marsh suspects is a dig.

years.big: "This is rubbish. Get Nick to play it."
years.h: Rocco Barker walks out of the Sydney sessions
years.p: Producer Mark Opitz brings Plastic Fantastic to INXS's Rhino Studios. After two days on 'Decline and Fall', Barker says, Mills listens for four bars and says that. Barker goes drinking and doesn't come back.
years.xp:
Everyone was fraying. Mills calls himself a control freak who "lost the dressing room"; Mitchell, told he had an old back injury, started going to the gym, which Marsh thought wasn't very rock'n'roll. Greening wrote much of the record and, under his deal, kept his royalties rather than splitting them four ways.

"We were top of college radio in America," Mitchell says, "and then we went to Sydney and it all blew up in our faces."

eras.title: A PiL tour, a phone call and a split
eras.text: Just before the biggest tour they'd ever booked, the band split in two. The singles kept climbing American alternative radio while the band fell apart around them.

years.h: Marsh fires Mills and Mitchell on the eve of the PiL tour
years.p: Mills has just booked a US and Canada support run with [[Public Image Ltd|68950696-ee9a-49b2-a8c2-d1d6c19355cc]]. Then Marsh calls: he doesn't want to work with Mills or Mitchell any more.
years.xp:
Accounts differ. Barker doesn't think anyone was sacked; he remembers telling Marsh he was quitting, and Marsh saying he'd quit too. Marsh told Vive Le Rock the same story the other way round. "I was basically sacked from my band," Mitchell says. "The band that I started."

A cease-and-desist and legal squabbles followed, according to Louder.

years.h: Plastic Fantastic cost £400,000, Mills says
years.p: Out in the US first, Britain four months later. 'Decline and Fall' goes top 15 on Billboard's new Modern Rock chart.

years.cap: Flesh for Lulu with Derek Greening (second left), c. 1989
years.h: John Lydon draws on Rocco Barker's shirt, and it ends in the gutter
years.p: On the PiL tour Lydon takes a marker to Barker's silk shirt. Barker answers with a lit Marlboro on Lydon's tracksuit, and a fight spills into the street.
years.xp:
Barker's account: Lydon swung, missed and hit Barker's girlfriend, March Violets singer Cleo Murray. Next day at soundcheck PiL applauded him, and John McGeoch said it was about time somebody did that.

At the last show in LA, Barker says, Lydon found him backstage: "You do forgive me, don't you?"

years.h: Del Strangefish's 'Time and Space' is their biggest US hit
years.p: It reaches the Modern Rock top 10. Marsh hated it, and later told Vive Le Rock the label loved it.

years.h: 'She Was' hits No. 9, then Capitol drops them
years.p: It's another Modern Rock top 10 and a track on a Nintendo compilation. A Hollywood Records deal falls through after Capitol lets them go.

years.src: Wikipedia: Flesh for Lulu · Louder · flesh4lulu.co.uk
years.h: Flesh for Lulu quietly announce the end
years.p: Marsh blamed musical differences, "two separate trains of thought". Barker and Marsh pop up on Peter and the Test Tube Babies' Stock Aitken Waterman covers album first.

eras.title: Gigantic, a re-recording and a funeral march
eras.text: Marsh and Barker had one more go at the big time under a new name, then went separate ways. Marsh found a home in the Urban Voodoo Machine, revived Flesh for Lulu twice, and kept singing until the end.

years.h: As Gigantic, Marsh and Barker sign to Columbia and open for Bush
years.p: They make an album, Disenchanted, with Tim Palmer in LA, and tour with [[Bush|93ccd76c-3790-4435-a8bf-02bc26294b93]] and the Goo Goo Dolls. Marsh said it was dropped before it came out.
years.xp: Marsh's version: the A&R man who signed them, Nick Terzo, left the label, and Gigantic went with him. Music for Nations signed and dropped them too, and the band ended in 1998.

years.h: Marsh's solo album A Universe Between Us
years.p: Produced by Katharine Blake of the Mediaeval Baebes, who becomes his partner. Since 2003 he's also been singing with the Urban Voodoo Machine.

q: It's a bit of a middle-finger up to the record industry.
years.h: The hits re-recorded, so the labels don't get paid
years.p: The Best of Flesh for Lulu is all new recordings, plus the single 'Cold Flame', written by Barker in the '80s.

years.cap: Will Crewdson, Mark Bishop and Nick Marsh at Leeds O2 Academy, October 2013
years.h: A new Flesh for Lulu opens for the Goo Goo Dolls in Britain
years.p: With Will Crewdson in for Barker, Mark Bishop on drums and Keith McAndrew on bass, Marsh plays packed rooms on the UK tour, Hammersmith Apollo included.

years.src: Louder · AV Club · Wikipedia: Flesh for Lulu
years.h: Nick Marsh dies of mouth and throat cancer at 53
years.p: Diagnosed in 2014, he'd played a last London show at the Brooklyn Bowl in March. At his funeral in Epping Forest, the Urban Voodoo Machine led the procession as a marching band.
years.xp:
Marsh wrote about his treatment openly on Facebook. At the Brooklyn Bowl, Crewdson says, Marsh sang the closing line of 'Sleeping Dogs' twice, something he'd never done.

His last album, From the Deep, made with Katharine Blake, came out that October.

sources.title: Louder: The epic story of Flesh for Lulu
